page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne.8xlarge is a high-density local storage instance provisioned on KVM hypervisors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 128 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4 GB RAM per core. A key feature is its massive local storage capacity, offering 94,489 GB of local hard disk drive space paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

The server is tailored for high-capacity local storage tasks rather than high IOPS or compute-heavy processing. While the Intel Broadwell-based Xeon E5-2682v4 provides reliable dedicated processing across 32 vCPUs, it lacks modern instruction sets like AVX-512, AMX, or specialized hardware cryptography extensions. Given the reliance on rotational HDD media rather than high-speed NVMe storage, throughput is optimized for sequential data access patterns and long-term retention rather than low-latency random reads and writes.

This hardware profile offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for scenarios requiring massive local storage volume alongside moderate compute and memory resources. It is suited for big data processing frameworks, distributed file systems, data warehousing, log analytics, cold storage archives, and large-scale backup nodes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne.8xlarge is a storage-focused cloud instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs based on the 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor and x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 128 GB of system memory and 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, its defining hardware characteristic is a massive 94,489 GB local HDD storage capacity. The server utilizes a KVM hypervisor and delivers a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU core. Due to its reliance on rotational HDD local disks and older Broadwell architecture without modern vector extensions, the instance prioritizes bulk volume storage efficiency over high-IOPS or compute-intensive operations. The ecs.d1ne.8xlarge provides strong resource density for sequential data ingestion, log analytics, distributed file storage, and data archiving workloads.
